title: Fine Arts Handbook: Who May Check Out a District Instrument, the Usage Agreement and Condition Reports
content:
This section of the Fine Arts Handbook states the requirements for a checkout under the Fine Arts Instrument Usage Program.

## Requirements

**Enrollment and ensemble.** An instrument is checked out only to a student whose district enrollment record is in status provisional or enrolled and who is scheduled in an ensemble course listed in the usage type's required ensemble courses; a Summer Instrument Checkout requires enrollment in the ensemble for the next school year.

**Agreement and assignment.** The parent signs the instrument usage agreement and the ensemble director approves and assigns the instrument by ensemble need; families do not choose a specific instrument.

**Condition reports.** The director records a condition report at checkout and at return using the program's condition grades, and damage at return is judged against the checkout report.

**Student-supplied items.** Items listed as student-supplied for the usage type are bought by the family and are never loaned.

## What decides the enrollment requirement

The enrollment requirement is read from the system's records before the checkout, not from what the family says about the student. The record is the student's own district enrollment record, matched to the student who would receive the instrument; its status must be provisional or enrolled. A status other than these two does not meet the requirement.

| Student's district enrollment record | Scheduled in a listed ensemble course | Meets the enrollment and ensemble requirement |
|---|---|---|
| provisional | yes | yes |
| enrolled | yes | yes |
| provisional | no | no |
| enrolled | no | no |
| any other status | yes | no |
| any other status | no | no |

For a Summer Instrument Checkout, enrollment in the ensemble for the next school year is required.

## Hypothetical cases

1. A student's enrollment record is provisional and the student is scheduled in band. Under a band usage type the student meets the enrollment and ensemble requirement.
2. A student is scheduled in orchestra, and the family asks for a Woodwind Instrument Usage checkout, whose listed course is band. The student is not scheduled in a listed course, so the requirement is not met for that usage type.
3. A family asks for a particular serial-numbered violin. The director assigns the instrument by ensemble need; the family does not choose a specific instrument.
4. A clarinetist's family asks to borrow reeds with the instrument. Reeds that are listed as student-supplied are bought by the family and are never loaned.
5. An instrument graded good at checkout comes back with a dent. The director records the return condition report, and the damage is judged against the good grade on the checkout report.
